title: Resilience and Recovery

header.html: 3.4 Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1The goal

Resilience keeps services running when something fails; recovery brings them back after an outage or attack. Both protect availability (the "A" in CIA).

2Recovery sites

Site State Recovery speed Cost
Hot site Fully equipped and running, data kept current Minutes to hours Highest
Warm site Equipment ready, data needs restoring Hours to days Medium
Cold site Empty space with power and connectivity Days to weeks Lowest

Also consider environmental factors (power, cooling, floods, location) when choosing a site.

Exam tip

. Hot = fastest and most expensive; cold = slowest and cheapest; warm = in between. The choice follows the recovery time objective.

3Platform diversity and redundancy

Strategy Meaning
Platform diversity Use different vendors, hardware and virtualization so one flaw or outage does not hit everything
Load balancing Spreads traffic across servers
Clustering Servers work together and take over if one fails
Autoscaling Adds or removes capacity automatically with demand
High availability (HA) Design with no single point of failure
Multicloud systems Run across more than one cloud
Power UPS (battery), redundant power supply (RPS), generator, surge protector
Storage RAID and replicated storage Beyond the objectives
Exam tip

. UPS bridges a short outage; a generator covers a long one. Clustering gives automatic failover; load balancing shares load and can remove failed nodes.

4Backups

Topic Key points
Retention How long backups are kept (legal and business needs)
Immutability Backups that cannot be changed or deleted for a set time: protect against ransomware
Scope What is backed up: full, incremental (changes since the last backup of any type), differential (changes since the last full)
Restoration testing Test restores regularly: an untested backup is not a backup
Offline and offsite copies Keep a copy away from the network and in another place

A common rule is 3-2-1: 3 copies, on 2 types of media, 1 offsite. Beyond the objectives

5Testing, planning and metrics

Item Meaning
Testing Failover tests, simulation and parallel processing (run the recovery system alongside production)
Disaster recovery (DR) Restore IT systems after a major event
Business continuity (BC) Keep the business running during and after a disruption
Capacity planning Ensure enough people, technology and infrastructure for the future
Metric Meaning
RTO (recovery time objective) Maximum time a system can be down
RPO (recovery point objective) Maximum data loss measured in time (how old the last backup may be)
MTTR (mean time to repair) Average time to fix a failure
MTBF (mean time between failures) Average time a system works between failures

Exam tip

. RTO = how long down. RPO = how much data you can lose. If backups run every 4 hours, the RPO is up to 4 hours. Higher MTBF is better; lower MTTR is better.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors must resume operations within one hour after a disaster and can afford a fully equipped duplicate site. Which site fits?

  • AHot site
  • BCold site
  • CWarm site
  • DAir-gapped site
Show the answer

Answer: A. A hot site is fully equipped and current, giving the fastest recovery.

S2A company backs up every 6 hours. What is the best description of its RPO?

  • AThe system can be down 6 hours
  • BA repair takes 6 hours on average
  • CUp to 6 hours of data could be lost
  • DA failure happens every 6 hours
Show the answer

Answer: C. The RPO is the amount of data loss tolerated, which depends on the backup interval.

S3Which backup feature helps most to protect against ransomware that tries to delete backups?

  • ADeduplication
  • BCompression
  • CImmutability
  • DEncryption in transit
Show the answer

Answer: C. Immutable backups cannot be changed or deleted for a set time, so ransomware cannot destroy them.

S4A data center loses power for 20 seconds before the generator starts. Which device keeps servers running in that gap?

  • ASurge protector
  • BLoad balancer
  • CSwitch
  • DUPS
Show the answer

Answer: D. A UPS provides battery power for short outages until the generator takes over.

S5Which test runs the recovery environment next to production without switching users to it?

  • AFull failover
  • BTabletop exercise
  • CRestoration of one file
  • DParallel processing
Show the answer

Answer: D. Parallel processing runs the recovery system alongside production to check it without disruption.

S6A team measures the average time a server runs before it fails. Which metric is this?

  • AMTBF
  • BMTTR
  • CRTO
  • DRPO
Show the answer

Answer: A. Mean time between failures is the average operating time between failures.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which recovery site is cheapest and slowest?

Show the answer

A cold site.

R2What does RTO measure?

Show the answer

The maximum time a system may be down.

R3What does RPO measure?

Show the answer

The maximum acceptable data loss in time.

R4What is the difference between disaster recovery and business continuity?

Show the answer

DR restores IT systems; BC keeps the business running.

R5What is platform diversity?

Show the answer

Using different vendors or platforms so one failure does not affect everything.

R6Why test restores?

Show the answer

To prove that backups actually work.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Sites hot (fast, costly), warm (middle), cold (slow, cheap)
Redundancy load balancing, clustering, autoscaling, HA, multicloud; UPS, RPS, generator, surge protector
Backups retention, immutability, scope (full, incremental, differential), restoration testing
Plans and tests failover, simulation, parallel processing; DR vs BC; capacity planning
Metrics RTO (downtime), RPO (data loss), MTTR (repair time), MTBF (time between failures)
